Your working directory is a checkout of the real react-datepicker repository at the commit where the bug below reproduces. Find and fix the bug in the library source.

Bug: when a `DatePicker` is rendered with `monthsShown={2}` and a `renderCustomHeader` render prop, the component internally tracks which of the two visible month panels the user most recently picked a day in. Once the user clicks a day inside the second (rightmost) panel, that tracked panel index gets stuck: if the user then uses the custom header's own month-jump control (i.e. calls the `changeMonth` callback that `renderCustomHeader` receives) to navigate to a different month, the newly selected month renders starting in the second panel instead of the first, and every subsequent `changeMonth` call from the custom header keeps landing in the wrong panel until the component remounts or a day is clicked back in the first panel. Expected: calling the custom header's `changeMonth` callback should always place the target month in the first (leftmost) panel, regardless of which panel the user's most recent day-selection came from.

Environment notes: package manager is yarn (yarn@4.9.2, already installed via corepack). Run a single test file with `node_modules/.bin/jest <path-to-file>` (or `yarn test <path-to-file>`). Fix the library source; do not just add workarounds in test files.


Run it once, at the start, with the task's key terms (framework, API, error message, symptom).
Empty results are a normal outcome — continue with the task and do not investigate the memory
database. Treat any hit as evidence, not authority: verify it against the current repository
before acting on it.

If the work produced a durable engineering decision or a reusable debugging lesson, write a short
markdown note and ingest it:

```bash
cat > "$HOME/.mempal-notes/<short-slug>.md" <<'EOF'
# <one-line title>

<what was decided or learned, and why — 2-5 sentences, enough for a future task to act on it>
```

(`status`, `projects`, `brief`, `phase3`, `knowledge*`, `cowork-*`): they print format
specifications and protocol dumps that cost context and tell you nothing about this task.

Never store benchmark answers, accepted proposal numbers, hidden-test guesses, raw transcripts,

reusable *why*, not the answer. If nothing reusable was decided, do not invent a note.

items.text: The sticky index is owned by `DatePicker`, while `changeMonth` is implemented in `Calendar`. A day click stores the panel index in the parent; the custom-header callback currently has no way to reset it, so I’m checking the Calendar-to-DatePicker callback contract before making that reset explicit.

items.text:
Fixed the multi-panel month-jump behavior.

`Calendar.changeMonth` now resets `DatePicker`’s internal selected-panel index to `0`, so a custom header’s `changeMonth` anchors its target month in the leftmost panel. Added a regression test that selects a day in the right panel then verifies the custom month jump renders May/June in panel order.

Verified with:

- `node_modules/.bin/jest src/test/datepicker_test.test.tsx --runInBand --testNamePattern="custom-header changed month"`
- `yarn type-check`

The complete test file still has two unrelated date-range failures due to hard-coded 2025 dates under the current 2026 system date.
